rationale: Both role-isolated advisory inputs were present from distinct runs and model families, pinned to the same frozen candidate. The academic review returned request-changes with one blocking, four major and two minor findings; the learning-design review approved. The blocking finding was the decisive one: the clinical wrap-up issued a documentation and information-sharing instruction that none of its sources supported and that varies by jurisdiction, employer policy and a risk assessment the scene never performs. It was resolved by removing the instruction rather than by sourcing it, because a lesson explicitly scoped away from clinical authority should not be answering that question at all. The remaining findings were bounded corrections to a source's currency, a misread pair of survey items, two answer keys, a sorting heuristic and one counterfactual, and were repaired in the same single finalization pass. The academic verdict stands as dissent; no reviewer has seen the repaired text.
dissent: The academic review's request-changes verdict stands as material dissent from the candidate as reviewed, including its blocking finding. That finding was incorporated by removing the prescribed answer; no reviewer has approved the result.
conditions: The repaired content is committed first and that commit is stamped as finalCommit, with no teaching-content change afterward.
Strict source preflight and full validation must pass on the final content before merge.
The publication transition is the maintainer's separate act and is not authorised by this decision.
